title: Technology Assessment, Techno-Economic Evaluation and Risk Analysis of Dynamic Line Rating for Overhead Transmission Lines: A PRISMA-Based Systematic Literature Review
content: Dynamic line rating (DLR) adapts the ratings of overhead lines to actual or forecast weather and conductor conditions, supplementing or replacing conservative static line ratings (SLRs) when conditions allow. Utilities must judge their maturity, economics and risks together. This systematic review, reported following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020, retrieved 1234 records from IEEE Xplore, Scopus, SpringerLink and supplementary searches with the AI-assisted tool Consensus; 363 studies published in 2010–2026 were included and coded into technology assessment (n = 142), techno-economic evaluation (n = 156) and risk/reliability assessment (n = 145). Field studies in temperate, wind-exposed systems report gains commonly cited at 20–40% (5–10% for ambient-adjusted ratings), whereas tropical studies report smaller margins and ratings below the SLR during heat waves. System-level simulations report operating-cost reductions of about 3–16%, but DLR-specific costs are rarely itemised. Only 3 studies were coded as addressing all three dimensions, and cost–benefit analyses with explicit risk quantification are rare. Twelve deployment and operational risks were consolidated into a literature-informed likelihood–consequence matrix, in which rating overestimation and unaccounted low-wind/heat-wave conditions ranked highest. A conceptual five-stage framework is proposed to help utilities, particularly in tropical power systems, move from line screening to risk-informed deployment decisions.
